[0] iOS 27 brings several new features to Apple's Photos app, including two long-awaited additions: a full-featured slideshow maker and an upgraded version of iCloud Shared Albums.

[1] #1: Full-feature slideshow maker

[2] The Photos app has long offered a very basic slideshow feature, but it has been primarily designed for reliving personal memories. If you wanted to create a slideshow for an event or another public occasion, you had to look elsewhere.

[3] But in iOS 27, Photos finally gets a comprehensive suite of slideshow creation tools.

[4] You can now present any group of photos or videos as a slideshow, with customizable transition styles, display duration, and background music. You can also set it to loop automatically and even save the slideshow as a video file for later viewing.

[5] A full-featured slideshow capability is long overdue in the Photos app, and I'm thrilled it has finally arrived.

[6] #2: Shared Albums upgrade

[7] You may not know that the Photos app actually includes a built-in, social network-like feature: Shared Albums.

[8] iCloud Shared Albums lets you create an album to share with friends or family. You receive activity updates showing newly added photos and videos, and you can like or comment on any shared content. The feature resembles an old-school version of Instagram, but it's private—only the people you choose can participate.

[9] I love this feature, and iOS 27 brings some long-awaited upgrades. You can now share full-resolution photos and videos (previously lower resolution), react using any emoji, set new participant permissions, and Android and Windows users can now also join the album.

[10] The Shared Albums improvements arrive at just the right time, coinciding with the launch of Apple's new HomePad device, and these upgrades make me even more excited about that product.
